# 1 Chronicles Chapter 13 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folio 378r

---

**13:1** And-consulted [vayyiva'ats] David with the-commanders of-the-thousands and-the-hundreds, with-every leader [nagid]. **13:2** And-said David to-all the-assembly [qehal] of-Yisra'el: If upon-you [it is] good, and-from YHWH our-God, let-us-send-out [nifretshah] — let-us-send to our-brothers [acheynu] the-remaining [ha-nish'arim] in-all the-lands of-Yisra'el, and-with-them the-priests [ha-kohanim] and-the-Levi'im in-the-cities of-their-pasturelands [migrasheyhem], and-let-them-gather [yiqqavetsu] to-us. **13:3** And-let-us-bring-around [nasibbah] the-ark [aron] of-our-God to-us, for not did-we-seek-it [derashenuhu] in-the-days of-Sha'ul.

**13:4** And-said all the-assembly to-do so, for the-thing [was] right [yashar] in-the-eyes of-all the-people. **13:5** And-assembled [vayyaqhel] David all Yisra'el, from-Shichor of-Mitsrayim and-to Levo-Chamat, to-bring the-ark of-God [ha-Elohim] from-Qiryat-Ye'arim. **13:6** And-went-up David and-all Yisra'el to Ba'alah, to Qiryat-Ye'arim which [belongs] to-Yehudah, to-bring-up from-there the-ark of-God, YHWH, who-sits [yoshev] [upon] the-cheruvim [ha-keruvim], where is-called the-Name [ha-Shem].

**13:7** And-they-carried [vayyirkhevu] the-ark of-God upon a-new cart [agalah chadashah] from-the-house of-Avinadav, and-Uzza and-Achyo [were] driving [nohagim] the-cart. **13:8** And-David and-all Yisra'el [were] celebrating [mesachakim] before God [ha-Elohim] with-all strength [be-khol oz] and-with-songs [be-shirim] and-with-lyres [be-khinnorot] and-with-harps [bi-nevalim] and-with-tambourines [be-tuppim] and-with-cymbals [bi-metsiltayim] and-with-trumpets [u-va-chatsotsrot].

**13:9** And-they-came to the-threshing-floor [goren] of-Kidon, and-put-forth [vayishlach] Uzza his-hand to-seize [le-echaz] the-ark, for the-oxen [ha-baqar] stumbled [shametsu]. **13:10** And-burned [vayyichar] the-anger [af] of-YHWH against-Uzza, and-he-struck-him [vayyakkehu] because [asher] he-put-forth his-hand upon the-ark, and-he-died there before God [lifnei Elohim].

**13:11** And-it-was-displeasing [vayyichar] to-David because YHWH had-broken-forth [parats] a-breach [perets] against-Uzza, and-he-called that place Perets-Uzza, unto this day. **13:12** And-feared [vayyira] David God [ha-Elohim] on-that day, saying: How shall-I-bring to-me the-ark of-God?

**13:13** And-not did-remove [hesir] David the-ark to-himself, to the-city of-David, and-turned-it-aside [vayyattehu] to the-house of-Oved-Edom the-Gitti. **13:14** And-remained [vayyeshev] the-ark of-God with the-house of-Oved-Edom, in-his-house, three months. And-blessed [vayevarekh] YHWH the-house of-Oved-Edom and-all that [was] to-him.

---
## EMET's Textual Notes

**v.3 — lo derashenuhu:** "We did not seek it" — the verb *darash* (to seek/inquire) connects back to Saul's failure to *darash* YHWH (10:14). David's first royal act corrects Saul's central failure. The ark represents the presence of God that Israel neglected under the previous regime.

**v.6 — yoshev ha-keruvim:** "Who sits [upon] the cherubim" — this is the divine throne title. The ark is not merely a religious artifact but the footstool/throne of the invisible God.

**v.7 — agalah chadashah:** "A new cart" — this is the method the Philistines used (1 Sam 6:7). The Chronicler will later explain (15:13) that the failure was procedural: they did not carry it as the Torah prescribes (by Levitical poles).

**v.9 — goren Kidon:** "Threshing floor of Kidon" — 2 Samuel 6:6 has "Nachon." The Chronicler uses a different name; *kidon* means "javelin" or "destruction."

**v.10-11 — perets:** The wordplay is central — YHWH *parats* (broke forth) against Uzza, and the place is named *Perets-Uzza*. The same root *p-r-ts* will recur when David learns to do things properly (14:11).

*— EMET*
